hook.text: Your Uber driver's car moves on the map in real time. Millions of drivers send GPS updates every 4 seconds.

buildup.text: Each driver sends latitude, longitude, speed, and heading. The system ingests millions of location events per second.

discovery.text: Uber uses Apache Kafka to ingest location streams and stores them in a geospatial database for fast proximity queries.

twist.text: GPS is noisy. A driver appears to jump between buildings. Snap-to-road algorithms correct position to the actual road.

climax.text: Real-time location tracking needs high-throughput ingestion, geospatial indexing, and noise correction at scale.

punchline.text: Millions of GPS pings per second — ingest, index, and correct.

quiz.question: Why do ride-sharing apps need snap-to-road algorithms?
options: GPS is noisy and shows cars in wrong locations that need correcting
